content.value_statement: Robotics learners need clear guidance across ROS 2, simulation, perception, and control. This skill explains core concepts and supports structured robotics study.
actual_capabilities: Explains Physical AI, embodied intelligence, ROS 2, SLAM, inverse kinematics, and reinforcement learning.
Provides ROS 2 Python and C++ example guidance for educational use.
Maps textbook topics into modules, labs, and capstone project planning.
Helps troubleshoot robotics simulation concepts in Isaac Sim and Gazebo.
Connects perception topics such as object detection and segmentation to robot workflows.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, datasets, or simulator assets.
Cannot verify robot hardware safety or real-world deployment readiness.
May need project-specific package files to debug build errors.
Focuses on educational guidance, not certified robotics engineering review.

output_examples.input: Explain SLAM to a first-year robotics student.
output: Defines SLAM as building a map while estimating robot position.
Explains sensors, landmarks, uncertainty, and loop closure.
Ends with a short checklist for common beginner confusion.

output_examples.input: Help plan a ROS 2 Humble lab for publishers and subscribers.
output: Lists learning goals, required packages, node roles, checks, and expected observations.
Adds troubleshooting notes for topic names, message types, and launch files.

output_examples.input: Recommend a simulator for a humanoid robot prototype.
output: Compares physics fidelity, visual realism, ecosystem support, and setup complexity.
Recommends a simulator based on project goals and team experience.

best_practices: State the robot platform, ROS 2 version, simulator, and sensor stack before asking for help.
Ask for diagrams or stepwise explanations when learning control, mapping, or perception topics.
Separate conceptual questions from build errors so the response can target the right layer.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for deployment-ready robot safety approval from a general guidance skill.
Do not omit simulator, package, and error context when troubleshooting ROS 2 workflows.
Do not request copied textbook chapters or proprietary course materials.

faq.question: What robotics topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers ROS 2, Physical AI, simulation, SLAM, inverse kinematics, reinforcement learning, and robot perception.

faq.question: Can it help with ROS 2 code examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain Python and C++ ROS 2 patterns for learning and planning.

faq.question: Does it run robotics simulators?
faq.answer: No. It explains simulator workflows but does not include executable simulator assets or automation.

faq.question: Is it useful for humanoid robotics?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain concepts for humanoid control, perception, simulation, and capstone planning.

faq.question: Can it debug my specific robot project?
faq.answer: It can help reason through errors when you provide package details, logs, versions, and expected behavior.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
